title: SLO-aware quick-fail path with regional drain backoff (hotpatch)
author: Evan Cross
release_notes: Hotfix: introduce SLO-aware quick-fail path and regional drain backoff to reduce cascading outages during regional congestion. Backportable to patch stream.
description:
Motivation: We observed two incidents (see SUP-421) where a sudden regional capacity pressure caused long tail latency and a cascade of retries that amplified load across regions. Existing circuit break and shedder logic reacted too slowly for short-lived spikes, resulting in tenant starvation and slow recovery. This hotpatch introduces a SLO-aware quick-fail path (fast-fail on imminent SLO breach) coupled with a regional drain backoff that throttles graceful draining to avoid amplifying cross-region failover pressure.

Design summary: single continuous change set that adds: 1) a fast-fail decision inside request admission that evaluates tenant SLO headroom with a sub-ms check and returns an immediate SLO-fail response for requests unlikely to meet their latency SLO, 2) a regional drain backoff controller that staggers node draining and applies exponential backoff to cross-region redirect rates, 3) telemetry tags and a new metric slo.quickfail_rate and slo.drain_backoff_active for realtime monitoring, and 4) feature flag and per-tenant opt-outs to enable gradual rollout. The fast-fail is a best-effort deterministic heuristic (uses per-tenant moving-window p50/p95 and current queue length) and falls back to existing circuit-breaker decisions if data is stale.

Checklist: [x] Add fast-fail admission codepath; [x] Implement regional drain backoff controller; [x] Add unit + integration tests; [x] Add dashboards and alert rules; [x] Backport branch prepared for 1.12.x.

Risk and mitigation: Fast-fail can change observed client errors; mitigations include conservative defaults, per-tenant opt-out, and a feature flag gated by rollout percentage. The drain backoff changes router behavior; we tested in staging with mirrored traffic before merge.

Testing and validation: Unit tests added for decision logic and backoff timer. Integration test simulates a regional congestion spike with 5k qps and validates that quick-fail reduces tail latency and that cross-region redirect rate remains under configured cap. Post-merge canary: 1% of production traffic -> 10% after 15m if no SLO regressions -> 50% after 1h.

Related: ENG-2345 (design), SRE-98 (incident follow-up), SUP-421 (customer escalations). See design doc: https://linear.app/redwood/ENG-2345/slo-quick-fail-drain-backoff (internal).
commits_summary: 3 commits: 1) admission: add slo_headroom quick-check and fast-fail response; 2) controller: regional drain backoff scheduler + heuristics; 3) infra: metrics + dashboard + tests; each commit is small and focused with tests included.
